goal: Discover the virtual storage and connect to the export named in the inventory ticket.
context: Builds on inspecting block devices and identifying stable storage. The virtual initiator is the client that connects to network storage.

concepts.title: Find the target and its portal
concepts.text: The target name identifies a storage service. The portal is the address and port for connecting to it. The SendTargets request returns the advertised pairs. A portal may host several targets, and a target may be reachable through more than one portal. Use both parts of the pair shown in your ticket.

concepts.title: Separate a saved record from a connection
concepts.text: Discovery saves the returned pairs as local node records in this exercise. The -m option chooses a mode, such as node or session. Use -T for the target name and -p for its portal. Login opens a session to the selected pair. Until login succeeds, a listed node supplies no attached disk.

concepts.title: Compare the LUN and disk identity
concepts.text: A logical unit number (LUN) identifies an exposed device within a target. Two exports can both show LUN 0. List the session with SCSI details to find the disk name, then compare its WWN (world wide name) with the ticket. A Linux name like sdc can change on a real host.

worked.label: Discover one storage service
worked.explanation: The two rows use the same destination portal with different target names. Neither row indicates an active connection.

worked.label: Choose the portal in the ticket
worked.explanation: The discovery address can differ from the address used for login. Use the returned portal that the ticket specifies.

worked.label: Follow the disk from session to inventory
worked.explanation: The session shows LUN 0 attached as sdc. The lsblk row identifies sdc as 0x5000000000000095, the WWN in this example's ticket.

practice.title: Identify the two addresses
practice.action: Compare Discovery address and Required portal below. The inventory ticket tells you what must be attached after login.
practice.observe: The discovery address names the directory to query. Its response supplies the actual destination and port.

practice.title: Discover, connect and inspect
practice.action:
Discover the portal and compare saved nodes with current sessions.
$ iscsiadm -m discoverydb -t sendtargets -p 198.51.100.41:3260 --discover
$ iscsiadm -m node
$ iscsiadm -m session
Connect to the matching target and portal, then find its disk.
$ iscsiadm -m node -T iqn.2024-04.example.training:media -p 198.51.100.43:3261 --login
$ iscsiadm -m session -P 3
$ lsblk -o NAME,WWN
practice.observe: The session list is empty before login. After login, match the attached disk name in the session output to its WWN in the disk listing.

practice.title: Compare what passes
practice.action: Select Check configuration. Log out of the practice export using the same target and portal with --logout in place of --login. Check again, then log it back in and recheck.
practice.observe: The record remains after logout. The active session and its disk no longer satisfy the task until you log in again.

requirements: Save a node record for the supplied target and portal.
Connect to that export and verify the supplied LUN and disk WWN.

review.introduction: Teaches target/portal, records and sessions, then uses a third set of inputs for the worked explanation.
review.example: Separate simulated commands investigate the virtual initiator and include an intentional incorrect action with a retry.
review.assignment: Gives a precise storage ticket and grades connected identity and any required startup policy as distinct outcomes.

goal: Connect the required disk now and arrange its automatic login later while keeping the existing auxiliary session running.
context: Builds on connecting to an exact target and portal. The required and auxiliary node records are already saved. The auxiliary session is running and must stay connected.

concepts.title: Read the saved startup policy
concepts.text: The node record stores node.startup separately from any active session. Use --op show with the target and portal to see that value. The --op option selects an operation on the record. A manual node can be connected right now and still be absent from the automatic startup plan.

concepts.title: Update one record
concepts.text: Use --op update -n node.startup -v automatic for the required record. This policy says a configured iSCSI login service may select it at startup. Changing the record does not establish a new session and does not log out an existing one.

concepts.title: Check today and a clean start separately
concepts.text: You can log in to the selected node or request login for the automatic nodes. Compare the active session and disk, then use Preview automatic logins to see what a later start would select from saved policies. The preview does not modify sessions.

worked.label: Inspect the selected record
worked.explanation: This record says manual. Its current session is a separate fact.

worked.label: Allow automatic login
worked.value: iscsiadm -m node -T iqn.2023-06.example.demo:index -p 192.0.2.60 --op update -n node.startup -v automatic
worked.explanation: Only the selected record changes. Leave the other running session alone.

worked.label: Connect now and verify
worked.value:
iscsiadm -m node --loginall=automatic
iscsiadm -m session -P 3
lsblk -o NAME,WWN
worked.explanation: The active sessions show the original auxiliary disk plus the required disk. The startup preview selects only the required record.

practice.title: Inspect the supplied state
practice.action: Use iscsiadm -m node and iscsiadm -m session to see the saved records and the existing connection.
practice.observe: The manual auxiliary record already has a live session. The required record exists but does not have a session.

practice.title: Update the required record and connect
practice.action:
Change the required record. Open Preview automatic logins and check before connecting.
$ iscsiadm -m node -T iqn.2024-04.example.training:reports -p 198.51.100.63:3260 --op update -n node.startup -v automatic
Connect the automatic node, then verify the disk.
$ iscsiadm -m node --loginall=automatic
$ iscsiadm -m session -P 3
$ lsblk -o NAME,WWN
practice.observe: The preview changes first. The existing session stays connected. Login then adds the required disk.

practice.title: Check the separate results
practice.action: Select Check configuration again. Change the required record to manual using the same update with -v manual, and check. Restore automatic and check once more.
practice.observe: The required disk stays attached when you choose manual. Only the future startup requirement fails until you restore automatic.

requirements: Keep the original auxiliary session running without interruption and leave its startup policy manual.
Connect to the required target and verify the supplied LUN and disk WWN.
Save automatic startup for only the required export and confirm the startup preview selects it.
